decisions.reason: After several years without renewed market evidence, this specialized through-contact wafer appears too uncertain relative to its likely engineering and support burden, so its option value looks largely exhausted.
Because carrier wafers are tightly tied to the firm's core thin-wafer handling offer and cost little to keep available, management would preserve this option despite limited visible evidence.
As a flagship packaging-wafer development aligned with the firm's strategic move toward more complex semiconductor applications, it is worth keeping while uncertainty about demand still resolves.
This off-the-shelf brand is very close to the established glass and quartz wafer business and has low incremental carrying cost, so keeping it open offers favorable option value.
Glass-based circuit boards are comparatively distant from the firm's narrow core substrate business and would absorb scarce development attention, so management would likely abandon this option.
